source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Press load default,save and reboot.
3. Boot in BIOS,compare setting should matches SPEC.
4. Change BIOS all/random setting in this function,to non-default  setting.
5. Save and reboot.
6. Boot in BIOS and check your setting still exist.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. The default setting should matches SPEC."
2. No error log happen.
3. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
4. Check your set still exist.

original_test_intent: Update an intended firmware component with an approved image and verify the resulting firmware identity, activation, configuration disposition, boot/management health and recoverability.
original_method: The item names Update Image, but the Procedure and Criteria only load defaults, change an unspecified BIOS setting and verify persistence. They contain no firmware target, image, direction, verification, flash trigger, progress, activation or recovery step.
manual_activity: After correction, an engineer must approve and operate the supported BIOS update UI/commit and monitor any platform-specific activation/recovery. The agent cannot infer or authorize the flash from the generic source.
required_inputs: Vendor-signed compatible image, digest, signature, release notes and board/product mapping
Supported BIOS update path, exact commit trigger, protected-region/preserve policy and tool/engine version
Stable power, maintenance window, OOB/console and independent recovery/rollback package
Activation/reset sequence, expected configuration disposition and post-update acceptance
safety_requirements: Do not interpret generic setting changes, Save & Exit or Load Default as authorization to flash firmware.
Never use an unidentified, unsigned, incompatible or wrong-target image, and never invent a vendor command.
Verify stable power, recovery independence and rollback constraints before any staging or write.
Define protected regions and whether settings, keys, serial data, inventories or update counters must be preserved.
Stop on verification failure, target mismatch, unexpected region plan, progress error, boot/management loss or recovery uncertainty.
No automatic retry, reflash or power cycle after failure.
agent_execution_scope: Before correction, preserve the source conflict and identify the missing update controls only.
After approval, verify public image metadata/digest/signature offline and collect read-only pre/post firmware identities, update logs, configuration diff, boot and management health.
Do not drive BIOS, stage/flash an image, decide activation/retry/recovery or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Replace the generic setting procedure with an approved vendor update lifecycle and align Criteria.
Approve image/target/direction/regions/preservation, power, activation and recovery; perform the firmware UI update.
Evaluate complete update, recovery and post-state evidence and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its manual boundary is valid, but the generic page-change workflow is not a firmware update method and must not be executed.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No command or update path is recommended until the owner/vendor supplies the exact supported workflow. Preserve the BIOS UI intent; do not substitute BMC, OS or third-party flashing.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The null script and 5/20-minute fields are preserved as source facts, but they do not define or authorize an update window.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define preflight compatibility/signature checks, exact BIOS selection and commit, monitored write/progress, activation/reset, version/region/configuration verification, health checks and a separately documented failure recovery path.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the exact board/component and vendor-supported BIOS update engine after correction.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record source/target BIOS/BMC/component versions, update-engine version, image digest/signature and recovery package version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor update and recovery documentation for the exact platform/component/image.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Introduces the entire missing firmware-update lifecycle rather than treating update as settings persistence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Restores the named update objective; current generic source has no valid update coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Target, images, direction, path, regions, power, activation, acceptance and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Rollback may be prohibited by anti-rollback or shared-component dependencies; vendor confirmation is required.

project_override_considerations: A project may supply an approved update direction, image and path, but must record the exact override and cannot claim the original generic procedure was completed. Formal firmware verdict remains engineer-owned.
expected_evidence: Corrected owner/vendor lifecycle, approvals, target/image identity and recovery
Pre-update firmware/configuration/health baseline and offline image verification
Operator BIOS path, commit/progress/activation evidence with stable-power controls
Post-update versions, regions/configuration, boot/BMC/OS health and original failure evidence
Recovery readiness/result as applicable and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items explicitly names a firmware update, whereas Procedure/Criteria define only a generic BIOS setting/default persistence cycle. The named destructive operation and supplied method/acceptance are different test intents.

blocked_analysis.analysis: No safe update operation can be derived because the target, image, commit, activation and recovery semantics are absent. This is a core operation conflict, not merely missing project parameters.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its manual BIOS boundary but rejects its generic setting sequence as non-equivalent to firmware update.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its vendor-image/recovery safeguards while strengthening classification to BLOCKED until the source lifecycle is corrected.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Prevents a destructive flash from being inferred through readiness inputs and preserves the named update intent.

review_improvement: Makes it impossible to claim firmware-update coverage from setting persistence and identifies every approval, identity, power, activation and recovery element required for a valid update case.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source omits the entire named destructive lifecycle. Since no safe operation or acceptance can be selected without inventing facts, the case is BLOCKED with SOURCE_CONFLICT.
no_automatic_retry: No update, reflash, retry, reset or recovery is authorized before lifecycle correction; after approval preserve first failure evidence and require engineer disposition before any further action.
